title: Finite pro-etale direct-image cohomology and its section augmentation
statement: Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $V=\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=V/\varpi^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $Y$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $f:Y\to s$, and use the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For $n\geq1$ let $F$ be any sheaf of $(A_n)_Y$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and let $C_F=\Gamma(s,Rf_{*,n}(F[0]))$, with K-injective direct image [def-weil-derived-direct-image] and exact point sections [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact]. There is a canonical $A_n$-linear isomorphism $\epsilon_F:F(Y)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^0(C_F)$, obtained from the nonnegative injective-resolution augmentation and the evaluation equality $(f_*F)(s)=F(Y)$ [def-weil-proetale-module-direct-image]. Every $H^j(C_F)$ with $j<0$ is zero. The maps $\epsilon_F$ are natural in module-sheaf morphisms. For $F=(A_n)_Y$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], the definitions of point evaluation and ordinary cohomology [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point, def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] identify $H^0(C_F)$ with the recorded $H^0(Y,A_n)$, and $\epsilon_F$ carries the section coming from $a\in A_n$ to the class defined by that same augmentation; in particular it carries the section $1$ to its unit class. No connectedness or nonemptiness of $Y$ is assumed.

proof.text: Put $A=A_n$ and $\mathcal M_Y=\Sh(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$. The size convention in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] supplies a small ringed site. By [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian] and [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives], $\mathcal M_Y$ is abelian with enough injectives. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-injective-resolution-degree-zero](1) to choose an augmentation $u_F:F[0]\to I_F^\bullet$ with injective terms and $I_F^r=0$ for $r<0$. This is K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective].

source.place: Tags 013K (lemma-injective-resolutions-exist), part (1), and 070J (lemma-bounded-below-injectives-K-injective); sites-cohomology.tex, Tag 07A5, introductory paragraph; injectives.tex, Tag 079H

proof.text: The same Grothendieck property gives K-injective resolutions of all complexes by [lem-sfb-grothendieck-k-injective]. Thus the arbitrary-resolution computation [lem-sf-kinjective-derived-map-computation], for the additive functor $f_*$ of [def-weil-proetale-module-direct-image], identifies the specified finite-level $Rf_{*,n}(F[0])$ [def-weil-derived-direct-image] with $Q(f_*I_F^\bullet)$. Exact point sections [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact] carry this isomorphism to $C_F\cong Q(J_F^\bullet)$, where $J_F^r=\Gamma(s,f_*I_F^r)=I_F^r(Y)$. Use these normalized comparisons for the following computations, including maps and changes of resolution.

source.place: Tag 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined); sites-cohomology.tex, Tag 07A5; direct-image construction and exact point evaluation

proof.text: Let $T=\Gamma(s,-)\circ f_*$. It is additive and left exact by [lem-weil-proetale-module-direct-image-left-exact] and [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-injective-resolution-degree-zero](2) to $T$ and $u_F$. It identifies $T(F)$ with $\ker(T(d_F^0))=H^0(J_F^\bullet)$. The direct-image evaluation formula [def-weil-proetale-module-direct-image] identifies $T(F)=F(Y)$. Consequently define $\epsilon_F(x)$ as the class $[u_F^0(Y)(x)]$, followed by the inverse of the normalized comparison $H^0(C_F)\cong H^0(J_F^\bullet)$. This is the asserted isomorphism. The augmentation, its cycle factorization and the comparison are morphisms of $A$-modules, so it is $A$-linear.

source.place: Tag 05TD (lemma-left-exact-higher-derived), part (3), last paragraph of proof: the exact sequence after applying a left exact functor

proof.text: Since $I_F^r=0$ for $r<0$, the sectionwise direct-image formula [def-weil-proetale-module-direct-image] gives $J_F^r=0$ there. For $j<0$, both the cycles in the zero module $J_F^j$ and the boundaries are zero. Hence $H^j(C_F)=H^j(J_F^\bullet)=0$.

source.place: Tag 05TD (lemma-left-exact-higher-derived), part (1); direct computation in the nonnegative resolution

proof.text:
For $h:F\to G$, [lem-weil-pbc-injective-resolution-lift-exists] supplies a chain map $v:I_F^\bullet\to I_G^\bullet$ satisfying $v^0u_F^0=u_G^0h$. The normalized derived-map formula [lem-sf-kinjective-derived-map-computation], followed by exact point sections [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact], represents $C_h$ by the chain map $v(Y)$. Thus on each section $x$,
$$H^0(C_h)(\epsilon_F(x))=[v^0(Y)u_F^0(Y)(x)]=[u_G^0(Y)h(Y)(x)]=\epsilon_G(h(Y)(x)).$$
Here the classes are read through the comparisons of Step 2. Applying this argument to $h=\mathrm{id}_F$ and any two chosen resolutions shows that their augmentations give the same map into $H^0(C_F)$: the derived-map formula identifies their transition with that same $v(Y)$. This proves naturality and independence of the resolution, hence canonicality.

source.place: Tags 013P (lemma-morphisms-lift), part (2), and 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined), with the augmentation equation evaluated in degree zero

proof.text: Take $F=A_Y$, the constant ring sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. At finite level, [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] defines point evaluation by $\Gamma(s,-)$, and [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] defines $H^0(Y,A)$ as the zeroth cohomology of this evaluated direct image. These definitions give $H^0(C_F)=H^0(Y,A)$. The section $a_Y$ induced by $a\in A$ therefore maps, by the formula of Step 3, to $[u_{A_Y}^0(Y)(a_Y)]$. This is precisely its augmentation class; taking $a=1$ gives the unit class. The argument applies to the zero sheaf and to empty or disconnected $Y$; it never identifies all constant-sheaf sections with $A$.
